data.gender_notes: Ijasvitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ijasvitha is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, which means 'Purity of Knowledge' or 'Goddess Isha'. In Hindu mythology, Isha is the goddess of sexuality, creativity, and fertility. This name is believed to bring blessings of purity, wisdom, and divine feminine energy. The name Ijasvitha carries the meaning “Purity, Knowledge, Goddess Isha” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ijasvitha usually hope their child will grow to embody purity, knowledge, goddess isha and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Blessing of divine feminine energy and creativity
data.etymology: Ijasvitha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Purity, Knowledge, Goddess Isha.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ijasvitha total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

Ijasvitha, also known as Prabhavatigupta, was a queen of the Gupta Empire during the 6th century CE. She is believed to have been a regent for her son Vikramaditya I, and was an influential patron of arts and culture during her reign.
